answers.answer: Shuffle Factory cards and place a face-down random number equal to players + 1 on the board; return the rest to the box without looking. Put one encounter token on each of the 11 marked territories. Randomly choose one structure bonus tile and place it face-up below the Popularity Track. The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.
answers.evidence: Setup: “number of players + 1”; “11 marked territories”; “Randomly choose one structure bonus tile”; “The lowest-numbered Player Mat starts.”

answers.answer: The Faction Mat sets starting power and combat-card draw; the Player Mat sets starting popularity, coins and two objective cards. On the map, place the character at home base and two workers, one on each of the two land-adjoined territories adjoining home. On the mats, place four mechs over Faction Mat abilities, six stars by the faction emblem, six technology cubes in Player Mat green boxes marked with a black square, four structures on matching Player Mat boxes, four recruits on bottom-row circular spaces, and the other six workers on Produce red rectangles. Put the action token beside the Player Mat ready for its first placement; leave one-time Faction Mat recruit spaces empty.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3–4 list which mat sets each starting value and the starting positions for all pieces.

answers.answer: You may take either action, both, or neither, but must move the token. Normally it must move to a different section; Rusviet may repeat a section. If taking both, top action comes first, and top-row gains may pay bottom-row costs. Pay all exposed red-box costs in full before choosing any amount of exposed green-box benefits; costs and benefits depend on the Player Mat and upgrades. You may decline benefits, but may not pay only part of a cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “may take either, both, or neither, but must move the token”; “bottom first is not allowed”; “pay the full cost” and “as much or as little” of benefits.

answers.answer: An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls that territory and its resources. Enemy units do not gain your structure's abilities; you keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill cannot produce on an uncontrolled territory. You may pay resource costs using resources from any territories you currently control, even when acting elsewhere.
answers.evidence: Control/resources: “An enemy worker alone on your structure's territory controls it and all its resources”; “You keep those abilities even without control, except the Mill”; resources from “any territories you currently control.”

answers.answer: No. A normal Move may move up to two different units one adjacent territory each, and the same unit cannot use both selections to move twice. A transported worker's carriage does not count as its own movement, so it may subsequently move itself; likewise, a worker may move onto a mech and be carried by the mech's later move. All units can carry any number of resources; only mechs can carry any number of your workers, and no unit carries your character.
answers.evidence: Move: “two different units”; “cannot use both selections to move the same unit twice”; carried worker movement and carrying limits.

answers.answer: Speed adds a territory of movement to the mech, but entering a territory with only enemy workers stops it and it cannot move again that turn. Those workers immediately retreat to their home base, leaving resources; the entrant loses one popularity per worker down to zero, and insufficient popularity does not prevent retreat. This is not combat. Your workers cannot independently enter a territory controlled by enemy workers.
answers.evidence: Move: “Your character/mech entering enemy workers only stops”; workers retreat; “Lose one popularity per worker, down to zero”; Speed's added step; workers cannot independently enter enemy-worker-controlled territory.

answers.answer: After all units finish the Move action, characters/mechs sharing a territory with opposing characters/mechs fight before a subsequent bottom-row action. The attacker chooses the order of multiple combats. A worker cannot independently move into or out of a territory controlled by enemy characters/mechs.
answers.evidence: Move: finish moving other units, then resolve combats “before the bottom-row action”; “attacker chooses multiple-combat order”; worker restrictions into or out of enemy character/mech-controlled territory.

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives two power or one combat card, before upgrades; if the combat deck is empty, shuffle discards into a new deck, and if both deck and discard are empty, draw none. Trade costs $1 and gives any two resources (same or different) or one popularity, before upgrades. Place traded resources on a controlled territory with at least one worker; you cannot Trade for resources if all your workers are at home.
answers.evidence: Bolster and Trade paragraphs give costs, choices, placement/home-worker restriction, and exhausted-deck handling.

answers.answer: Pay every exposed Produce cost (power, popularity and/or coins) in full before production. Then choose up to two different controlled territories; each worker there may produce one matching terrain token onto that same territory. New workers come from the Player Mat left to right and are placed in the producing village. You may decline some or all production, including new workers. Newly exposed costs apply to future Produce actions, not the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce steps 1–3 and follow-up: pay before production; new workers left to right; “You may decline”; exposed costs affect “future” actions.

answers.answer: Upgrade costs the number of oil tokens in exposed Upgrade cost boxes on your Player Mat; move a technology cube from a green box to an empty bracketed red box, improving a top benefit and reducing a bottom cost (solid-black-bordered red boxes cannot be upgraded). Deploy costs the number of metal tokens in exposed Deploy cost boxes; place a mech from your Faction Mat on a controlled territory with your worker, never a lake. Its uncovered ability then applies to your character and every mech, not workers. Even after completing all upgrades, mechs, structures and recruits, you may still pay for a bottom action to receive its coins and applicable ongoing recruit bonus.
answers.evidence: Bottom-row actions describe variable costs and placement/effects, then state completed actions may still be paid for coins and recruit bonuses. The rule about an equivalent with all exposed costs is not separately stated.

answers.answer: Build a structure on a controlled territory containing your worker; only one structure total may occupy a territory, including opponents' structures. The Factory is allowed, but lakes and home bases are forbidden. Structures cannot be moved or destroyed. A Mill gives a bonus production territory only while controlled; it can produce without an actual worker, and actual workers there also each produce. An uncontrolled Mill cannot produce. Your Mine is a personal tunnel for your units even when enemy-controlled; ordinary entry/combat restrictions still apply. Opponents cannot use your buildings' abilities.
answers.evidence: Build rules and structure effects: Mill works only while controlled; Mine is personal movement tunnel “even when enemy-controlled”; opponents cannot use buildings' abilities.

answers.answer: For Enlist, take a recruit from any bottom-row section of your Player Mat and place it permanently on any open one-time recruit bonus on your Faction Mat; immediately gain that chosen bonus: two power, two coins, two popularity, or two combat cards. The ongoing bonus is the circle uncovered where the recruit was removed, independent of the one-time choice. Ongoing bonuses trigger when you or either immediate neighbor takes that matching bottom-row action, not for top actions, encounters or similar Factory actions. Resolve active player first, then left neighbor, then right neighbor; stop if a sixth star ends the game. In two-player play the opponent triggers it once, not twice. Ongoing bonuses are Upgrade: one power; Deploy: one coin; Build: one popularity; Enlist: one combat card.
answers.evidence: Enlist and Ongoing recruits paragraphs specify destination, immediate bonuses, source of ongoing bonus, triggering actions, order, quantities and two-player treatment.

answers.answer: Combatants simultaneously and secretly choose dial power from zero to the lesser of seven and their current power. Each may add up to one combat card per participating character/mech, including at zero dial power; Rusviet People's Army adds one card if any workers are present. If both have combat mech abilities, attacker resolves theirs first, then defender. Reveal simultaneously and add dial and card values; attacker wins ties. Each player deducts their dial power from their track and discards every played combat card face-up; card values do not deduct additional track power.
answers.evidence: Combat steps 1–3 specify secret simultaneous dial choice, card limits, ability order, totals, tie rule and payment.

answers.answer: The winner controls the territory and its resources and places a combat star if eligible (normally at most two combat stars; Saxony has no usual limit within six available). All losing characters, mechs and workers retreat to their own home base, leaving all resources on the battle territory; Nordic Seaworthy may instead retreat eligible units and carried workers to adjacent lakes. A winning attacker loses one popularity per enemy worker forced to retreat, while a winning defender loses none; Polania Camaraderie has the stated combat exception. The loser draws one combat card if they revealed any power on the dial or through cards; a zero-total loser draws none.
answers.evidence: Combat step 4–5 gives the territory, star, retreat/resource, popularity and losing-card rules.

answers.answer: After the whole Move action and all combats, resolve the encounter if the character remains on the token territory; discard the token and draw a card before any following bottom action. If contested entry is lost, the character retreats and the encounter token stays. Resources, workers, mechs and structures gained go to the encounter territory. Pay the printed encounter cost, but no normal action cost applies and no mat benefits or ongoing recruit bonuses are gained.
answers.evidence: Encounters: after Move and “all combats”; contested loss leaves token; gains go to encounter territory; “no additional normal action costs” or mat benefits.

answers.answer: Every player's character must choose one available Factory card the first time that player finishes a Move action at the Factory (after winning any combat); return the rest. Each player gets at most one permanent card, and later visits cannot exchange it. The card is a fifth action section with optional top then bottom, under the usual no-repeat rule (Rusviet exception). Factory actions give no corresponding Player Mat coins, structure bonuses or ongoing recruit bonuses. Its bottom action moves one unit up to two territories within that Move action, or up to three for a Speed-enabled character/mech; Mine access and normal movement/stop restrictions apply.
answers.evidence: Factory section states each player's first finish, one permanent card, action-section use, no mat benefits, and bottom-action movement distances.

answers.answer: Only on your own turn, before or after completing a top or bottom action, may you reveal a completed objective. You may wait, but must meet all requirements at the moment you reveal it. Place the objective star and put both objective cards on the bottom of their deck. Normally only one objective star is allowed; Saxony keeps the second card after the first and can score both.
answers.evidence: Objectives and agreements paragraph specifies timing, requirements, both cards' destination and Saxony exception.

answers.answer: A star is earned for six upgrades, four deployed mechs, four built structures, four recruits, all eight workers on the board, one revealed completed objective, a combat victory (up to two stars), 18 popularity, or 16 power. Each goal is awarded once except the two combat stars and Saxony's exception. Stars are permanent after placement even if power or popularity later drops, and another player's star does not block a goal. The sixth star immediately ends play with no equalizing turns or further actions.
answers.evidence: Stars and immediate end lists all star goals, their once-only conditions, permanence, nonblocking, and sixth-star timing.

answers.answer: If a bottom-row action earns the sixth star, first collect its primary benefit, coins and ongoing recruit benefit, then place the star. For neighbor power/popularity recruit stars, finish the active action, then check active player first, left neighbor, right neighbor, checking for the sixth star each time; if an earlier player placed it, later recruit stars/bonuses do not resolve. If units remain intermingled in an unresolved battle, undo that part of movement and return initiating units to their origin territories; do not resolve another combat.
answers.evidence: Sixth-star sequence specifies collection before placement, active/left/right order and stopping condition, and undoing pending battle movement.

answers.answer: At 10 popularity, each star is worth $4, each controlled territory $3, and each complete pair of controlled resources $2. Five stars = $20; four ordinary territories plus Factory count as seven territories = $21; 13 resources make six pairs = $12, for $53 added to held coins. Also add the selected structure bonus, which is earned even if enemies control your structure territories; the summary does not specify which tile/features are present, so the amount of that bonus is unsupported. Ties after total coins go to most workers + mechs + structures (not character), then power, popularity, resources controlled, territories controlled, and stars placed.
answers.evidence: Final fortune table and example give $20 + $21 + $12 = $53; structure bonus section says it is earned despite enemy control; tie order is listed. The actual structure-bonus amount depends on the selected tile and qualifying features, which the question does not supply.
